page.layout: One page of verse in one column, italic type. Below the last line: a signature "C 4" at the centre foot and a catchword "Nam" at the right. No running head, no margin notes.

l.i: Ipse manu nobis vibrantem ex aethere flammam
Ecce quatit Deus, & felicia littora signat.
Vix ea cum coelum effulsit, tonitruque secundo
Signa dedit rerum Genitor, nam lapsus ab alto
Ductori caput innocuus circum dedit ignis,
Obstupuere omnes, tunc se se attollere tellus
Visa procul, sensimque humiles consurgere montes.
Ilicet excelsa Rodericus ab arbore signum
Dat prior, & terram repetita voce salutat
Terram omnes terram ingeminant, tormentaque
coeli Aemula dum flammam, & ventosa tonitrua miscet
Expediunt, una sonitum percussa remittunt
Aequora & insolito tremefacti murmure montes:
Quae Dux magne tuum tentabant gaudia pectus?
Quid tibi tunc animi? cum jam vicina videres
Littora tantorum studio quaesita laborum?
Nempe humilis taci to tecum sub corde volutas
Felices rerum eventus, acceptaque gratus
Cuncta Deo superisque refers, non coeca cupido
Imperij fastu tumefactum tollit inani,
Non auri rabies, & amor vesanus habendi
Jamque propinquabant Terrae jam carbasa Nautae
Demittunt malo, puppesque ad littora vertunt,
Cum Ductor lacrymans, salve o pulcherrima tellus
Nota mihi,
& fatis uni mihi debita tellus,
Quam propter certae potui me exponere morti
Ne precor externos ne dedignare colonos;

page.notes: The line "Nempe humilis taci to tecum" shows a space inside "tacito" in print; left as printed in the transcription above, possibly a printing or scan fault. "Quid tibi tunc animi? cum" has a doubtful mark after "animi". The page is set in italic, so no black letter is used. The word "Nam" at the right is the catchword of the next page. The "&" stands for the printed ampersand-like Et sign.
